name: Dyfed

attributes.attribute: name from the tribal name of the Demetae
reigns for a year in Dyfed
first codification of Celtic law in Wales

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dyfed was a Welsh region. It is also spelled Dyved. It lies in southwest Wales. Much of the action of the Mabinogiones happens there. The name comes from the tribal name of the Demetae. The Demetae were a Celtic tribe that lived there. Pwyll was the king of Dyfed. He married the goddess or heroine Rhiannon. She bore his child Pryderi in Dyfed. There she was punished for her perceived betrayal. Arawn was the lord of the Otherworld. He reigned in Dyfed for one year. He exchanged his rule with Pwyll. The change let Pwyll rid Ann pws of the king's strongest rival. The region also gave the first written Celtic law in Wales. These laws were the laws of Hywel Dda. The law took the king's name who encoded them.

okr.objective: Describe Dyfed as a Welsh region that hosts much of the Mabinogion action and early law.
